purpose: Perfluorohexyloctane is an eye drop used to treat dry eye disease. It helps relieve the uncomfortable symptoms of dry eyes, such as burning, stinging, grittiness, and blurry vision. It is especially helpful when the watery layer of your tears evaporates too quickly.
how_it_works: Your tears have an oily outer layer that helps prevent them from drying out too fast. In people with dry eye disease, this oily layer is often thin or disrupted. Perfluorohexyloctane acts like a synthetic oil layer on the surface of your eye, slowing down tear evaporation and keeping your eye moist and comfortable throughout the day.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are blurry vision right after putting the drops in (this usually clears up quickly), eye redness, eye discharge, and a mild stinging or burning sensation when first applied. Most side effects are mild and temporary.
warnings: This eye drop is for use in your eyes only — do not swallow it. If you wear contact lenses, remove them before using the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting your contacts back in. Tell your doctor if you notice any severe eye pain, sudden vision changes, or signs of an eye infection (increased redness, swelling, or discharge). Let your doctor know about all other eye medications you use.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one drop in each affected eye four times a day (about every 4 to 6 hours while you are awake). Try to space your doses evenly throughout the day. Always wash your hands before using eye drops, and avoid touching the tip of the bottle to your eye or any surface to keep it clean.
